subject: PrivStack module integration + CI playbook for partner on-prem bundles
messages:
From: Samira Patel <samira.patel@edgegrid.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-12T09:06:00Z
Subject: Intro — integrating Redwood PrivStack modules into EdgeGrid on-prem bundles

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking a call earlier. Per our discussion, EdgeGrid is preparing a 0.9.0 on-prem appliance bundle and we'd like to embed Redwood PrivStack modules for customers who want an integrated inference stack. We sketched an integration proposal and a minimal CI/validation flow to ensure upgrades are safe for offline customers.

Attached: edgegrid-priv-modules-proposal.pdf (proposal + topology diagrams).

High level asks from our side:
- A quick checklist of Terraform/Helm artifacts we must include from Redwood to keep the deployment immutable for air-gapped installs
- The recommended CI gates you expect (unit/infra tests, k8s manifests validation, image signing)
- Opinionated rollback steps if a module upgrade fails post-install

Can you point to the right contacts on your side for an IaC review and to align on the gating matrix? Samira and I are available next week for a short workshop.

Best,
Samira
Engineering Lead, EdgeGrid Solutions
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-12T11:02:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Intro — integrating Redwood PrivStack modules into EdgeGrid on-prem bundles

Looping in infra and private-deploy leads — Samira from EdgeGrid sent over a proposal (attached) and they want concrete CI/rollback guidance for embedding our PrivStack modules in an on-prem appliance.

Why this matters: if we ship module-level changes without clear gating or signed artifacts, EdgeGrid's air-gapped customers could be exposed to failed upgrades. We should give them a defendable baseline (Terraform/Helm contract, signed OCI images, preflight).

Primary asks for this thread:
1) Quick review of the proposal and a short list of must-have IaC artefacts (TF modules, Helm charts, values schema) — owner: lauren
2) CI gating matrix for partner appliance bundles (tests, attestations, signing) — owner: irene
3) Rollback and emergency cutover steps that EdgeGrid can automate — owner: markus

I attached a first-draft CI playbook to speed the discussion: ci-playbook-draft.md

Can we get a half-hour sync tomorrow 10:00-10:30 PT? If not, leave comments in the GitHub PR I created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/privstack/pull/198

Thanks — Jonas
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-12T13:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intro — integrating Redwood PrivStack modules into EdgeGrid on-prem bundles

Thanks Jonas — reviewed the proposal and the draft playbook. Quick inline notes (high level):

- Terraform: require explicit module version pins + a minimal locking file. For partner bundles we must produce a release artifact that includes a tfstate schema migration note when we change outputs. Add to the artifact: module-version.txt and sha256 checksums.
- Helm: supply both chart tarball and a values-schema.json that documents required vs optional values. In air-gapped installs we must include chart provenance files and signed tarball (cosign recommended).
- Values sanitization: add a preflight step that validates no disallowed network CIDRs or hostPaths are present. We'll publish a lightweight validator binary.

Gating matrix (short):
- Unit: module-level terratest for TF; chart lint + helm unit tests
- Integration: a k3s ephemeral cluster run with sample values + smoke tests against our health endpoints (10m job)
- Security: image scan + SBOM generation; cosign attestation check
- Acceptance: partner-specific baseline test that verifies LDAP/KMS integration works (edgegrid will supply test harness)

Rollback notes:
- Prefer immutable bundle approach — deploy previous fully-signed bundle rather than in-place module downgrade. If in-place is required, we need a documented sequence: disable feature toggles, apply previous TF plan with -target for state surgical changes, helm rollback for charts that support it, run data integrity checks.

I'll open a checklist PR against the privstack repo with the concrete files we should produce. Also please add any non-functional SLAs EdgeGrid expects in the PR description.

-- Lauren
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

1) Deliverables this sprint (owner -> due):
- checklist PR with file manifest and module_version.txt (lauren -> 2027-07-16)
- CI pipeline templates (GitHub Actions) with gates: unit/integration/security/acceptance (irene -> 2027-07-20)

2) Workshop: scheduled Wed 2027-07-21 16:00 UTC for partner-run test harness onboarding (Samira & EdgeGrid). Please prepare the sample k3s manifests and the validator binary.

3) Temporary measures for air-gapped installs: produce a fully self-contained bundle (charts, TF modules, images) with a single ZIP and a manifest.json + sha256sum file. EdgeGrid will host artifacts on their appliance repo.

Attachments: rollback-checklist.xlsx (ops steps + quick commands), ci-playbook-draft.md (latest draft).

Samira — thanks for the clear diagrams. We'll share the checklist PR and the action items before the workshop. If EdgeGrid has compliance constraints (FIPS, specific KMS), drop them in this thread and we'll call them out in the acceptance test matrix.

Irene
Head of Private Deployments Operations
Redwood Inference
